items.summary: Whisper is trained on 680,000 hours of labeled audio collected from audio-transcript pairs on the internet.

items.summary: Large V2 was trained for 2.5x more epochs and adds SpecAugment, Stochastic Depth, and BPE Dropout regularization.

items.summary: Robustness analysis uses LibriSpeech as the reference dataset and 12 other academic speech recognition datasets as out-of-distribution tests.

items.summary: Effective robustness (Taori et al., 2020) is used, measuring the difference in expected performance between a reference (in-distribution) dataset and out-of-distribution datasets.

locator.anchor: Section 3.3: 'effective robustness, introduced by Taori et al. (2020)'

items.summary: On VoxPopuli, Whisper significantly underperforms prior work and only beats the VP-10K+FT baseline.

locator.anchor: Section 3.4: 'On VoxPopuli, however, Whisper signiﬁcantly underperforms prior work and only beats the VP-10K+FT baseline from the original paper'

items.notes: Author-stated negative result. Suspected cause: other models use VoxPopuli distribution in pre-training and it has more supervised data.

items.summary: On Fleurs, log WER and log training-data-per-language have a squared correlation coefficient of 0.83; WER is estimated to halve for every 16x increase in training data.
items.conditions: Fleurs speech recognition; log-log linear fit, per-language

locator.anchor: Section 3.4 / Figure 3: 'strong squared correlation coefﬁcient of 0.83 ... WER halves for every 16× increase in training data'

items.summary: On CoVoST2 X->en, zero-shot Whisper achieves 29.1 BLEU (author-claimed new SOTA), attributed to 68,000 hours of X->en translation pre-training data vs CoVoST2's 861 hours; improves over mSLAM by 6.7 BLEU on the lowest-resource grouping.

locator.anchor: Section 3.5: 'a new state of the art of 29.1 BLEU zero-shot ... 68,000 hours of X->en translation data ... vastly larger than the 861 hours ... improving over mSLAM by 6.7 BLEU'

items.notes: 'state of the art' is an author claim (watch-list term); benchmark = CoVoST2, comparison set = Maestro/mSLAM/XLS-R, date context = Sep 2022. Text standardizer caveat noted by authors.

items.summary: X->en translation BLEU on CoVoST2 by resource group: Whisper 36.2 (high), 32.6 (mid), 25.2 (low), 29.1 (all); underperforms Maestro/mSLAM on high-resource.
items.conditions: Table 4; CoVoST2 X->en; BLEU by resource grouping

locator.anchor: Table 4: 'Zero-Shot Whisper 36.2 32.6 25.2 29.1'

items.notes: Whisper's High-resource 36.2 is below Maestro 38.2 and mSLAM 37.8 (author-stated underperformance).

items.summary: On Fleurs used as a translation benchmark, the squared correlation of log translation-data vs BLEU is only 0.24; Welsh is an outlier at 13 BLEU despite ~9,000 hours, traced to English audio mislabeled as Welsh.

locator.anchor: Section 3.5 / Figure 4: 'the squared correlation coefﬁcient is much lower ... only 0.24 ... Welsh (CY) is an outlier ... only 13 BLEU despite supposedly having 9,000 hours'

items.notes: Author-identified data-quality issue: majority of 'Welsh' translation data is English audio mis-classified by language ID.

items.summary: On Fleurs language identification, zero-shot Whisper reaches 64.5% accuracy, not competitive with supervised work (underperforms SOTA by 13.6%); accuracy upper-bounded at 80.4% due to 20 unseen languages, and 80.3% on the 82 overlapping languages.

locator.anchor: Table 5: 'Zero-shot Whisper 64.5'; Section 3.6: 'underperforms the supervised SOTA by 13.6% ... upperbounding accuracy at 80.4% ... On the 82 overlapping languages the best Whisper model achieves 80.3% accuracy'

items.summary: Zero-shot performance increases with model size across multilingual speech recognition, translation, and language ID, with diminishing returns for English speech recognition.

locator.anchor: Section 4.1 / Figure 8: 'With the exception of English speech recognition, performance continues to increase with model size'

items.summary: For small models trained with moderate compute, joint multitask/multilingual training shows negative transfer (underperforms English-only); at the largest scale the joint models outperform English-only counterparts.
items.conditions: Section 4.3 / Figure 9; adjusted for FLOPs on English speech recognition (only 65% of compute spent on English in joint training)

locator.anchor: Section 4.3 / Figure 9: 'for small models ... there is indeed negative transfer between tasks and languages ... eventually outperform models trained on English data only'; 'only 65% of compute is spent on this task'

items.summary: Whisper's text normalizer performs similarly to the independent FairSpeech normalizer on most datasets, but reduces WER significantly more on WSJ, CallHome, and Switchboard.
items.conditions: Section 4.4 / Figure 10; comparison of two normalizers

locator.anchor: Section 4.4 / Figure 10: 'on some datasets, namely WSJ, CallHome, and Switchboard, our normalizer reduces the WER of Whisper models' signiﬁcantly more'

items.notes: Author-noted risk that the normalizer could be overfit to Whisper's peculiarities.

items.summary: Whisper uses an off-the-shelf encoder-decoder Transformer; audio resampled to 16,000 Hz, 80-channel log-Mel spectrogram on 25 ms windows with 10 ms stride.

locator.anchor: Section 2.2: 'All audio is re-sampled to 16,000 Hz, and an 80-channel log-magnitude Mel spectrogram ... on 25-millisecond windows with a stride of 10 milliseconds'

items.summary: Tasks are specified via special decoder tokens; the model predicts language from a set of unique tokens (99 total) and quantizes timestamps to the nearest 20 ms.

locator.anchor: Section 2.3: 'a unique token for each language in our training set (99 total) ... quantizing all times to the nearest 20 milliseconds'

items.summary: Data pre-processing uses automated heuristics to remove machine-generated transcripts and an audio language detector (fine-tuned on VoxLingua107) to match spoken language to transcript language.

locator.anchor: Section 2.1: 'we developed many heuristics to detect and remove machine-generated transcripts ... an audio language detector ... on VoxLingua107'

items.summary: During development, Whisper models tended to transcribe plausible but almost always incorrect guesses for speaker names; addressed by brief fine-tuning on transcripts without speaker annotations.

locator.anchor: Section 2.4: 'Whisper models had a tendency to transcribe plausible but almost always incorrect guesses for the names of speakers'

items.summary: Whisper models are trained on 30-second audio chunks and cannot consume longer audio inputs at once, requiring a buffered/sliding-window strategy for long-form audio.

locator.anchor: Section 3.8: 'Whisper models are trained on 30-second audio chunks and cannot consume longer audio inputs at once'

items.summary: Remaining errors, especially in long-form transcription, include getting stuck in repeat loops, failing to transcribe the first or last words, and complete hallucination of unrelated text.

locator.anchor: Section 6 (Improved decoding strategies): 'getting stuck in repeat loops, not transcribing the ﬁrst or last few words ... complete hallucination'

items.summary: The pre-training dataset is very English-heavy; most languages have less than 1000 hours of training data, and speech recognition performance remains poor on many languages.

locator.anchor: Section 6 (Increase Training Data For Lower-Resource Languages): 'most languages have less than 1000 hours of training data'

items.summary: Only zero-shot transfer was studied; fine-tuning was not evaluated, and results may improve with fine-tuning where supervised data exists.

locator.anchor: Section 6 (Studying ﬁne-tuning): 'we have focused on the robustness properties ... only studied the zero-shot transfer performance'

items.summary: It is currently unclear to what degree Whisper's benefits stem from its encoder, decoder, or both; the impact of the language-model decoder on robustness was not ablated.

locator.anchor: Section 6 (Studying the impact of Language Models on Robustness): 'It's currently unclear to what degree the beneﬁts of Whisper stem from training its encoder, decoder, or both'

items.summary: A general trend of diminishing returns is observed when moving from 54,000 hours to the full 680,000-hour dataset; the full dataset yields only ~1 further point drop in English WER.

locator.anchor: Section 4.2: 'Using the full dataset, which corresponds to another 12.5× increase in size results in only a further 1 point drop in WER'

items.summary: The authors hypothesize that the human-machine gap arises from conflating in-distribution (machine) with out-of-distribution (human) generalization being measured on the same test.

locator.anchor: Section 3.3: 'We suspect a large part of this gap ... is due to conﬂating different capabilities being measured by human and machine performance'

items.summary: The authors suggest diminishing returns for English speech recognition (with model and dataset scaling) could be explained by saturation effects when approaching human-level performance.

locator.anchor: Section 4.1: 'diminishing returns for English speech recognition could be due to saturation effects from approaching human-level performance'

items.summary: Because models are trained for only 2-3 epochs, the authors assume over-fitting is not a large concern and use no data augmentation or regularization (for the original models).

locator.anchor: Section 2.4: 'Due to only training for a few epochs, over-ﬁtting is not a large concern, and we do not use any data augmentation or regularization'

items.notes: Large V2 later added regularization (see E008).
